questions.stem: Your code sets num_workers = 4 for a rostering solve, but the log's Parameters line reads only 'log_search_progress: true'. What does that tell you?

options.text: 4 is the default value, and default values are not listed on that line
options.says: The default of num_workers is 0 (every core), so a setting of 4 would be listed.

options.text: The line lists only logging settings, so the workers are in force
options.says: The GridCap log's line lists num_workers: 1 along with the logging settings.

options.text: The worker count is printed in the summary block, not on that line
options.says: The summary has no worker count; the parameters line is where a set num_workers shows.

options.text: The setting never reached the solver, or the line would show it
options.says: Right: the line lists every parameter not at its default, so a missing one was never set.

origin.section: The Header and Model Statistics Say What the Solver Was Given

questions.stem: A maximization stopped at its limit with no #Done line. Its #N lines raised best from 900 to 1,400, while its #Bound lines lowered the bound only from 1,610 to 1,600. Where did the run fall short?

options.text: Finding plans, as best stayed far below the bound throughout
options.says: The plans rose by 500 while the bound moved by 10; plans were found, the proof lagged.

options.text: Proving, as the bound fell by 10 while best rose by 500
options.says: Right: improving plans with a flat bound point to a weak bound, as in GridCap medium's one-worker log.

options.text: Nowhere, as a run with no #Done line still proved its last plan
options.says: #Done marks the end of a finished search; without it, a limit stopped the run.

options.text: Presolve, as a bound that starts at 1,610 means presolve was skipped
options.says: The first bound comes from the domains in every run; presolve ran before the search began.

origin.section: Each Progress Line Is an Event: a New Plan or a Better Bound

questions.stem: Two solves of a siting model log summaries with the same objective and the same model_fingerprint, but different solution_fingerprint values. What does that tell you?

options.text: The plans are the same, but the model changed between the solves
options.says: The model fingerprint is the same, so both solves had the same model.

options.text: One plan is wrong, as equal objectives give equal solution fingerprints
options.says: The solution fingerprint hashes the plan, and two different plans can have the same value.

options.text: The plans differ, and the two are worth the same amount
options.says: Right: equal solution fingerprints mean the same plan, so different ones mean different plans.

options.text: The plans are the same, as the solution fingerprint also hashes the clock
options.says: The fingerprint is a hash of the plan; times are reported separately as walltime and usertime.
